data.cli#Command line: go install github.com/go-theca/theca/cmd/theca@latest theca create vault.theca --size 1G # asks the password twice, prints the recovery code once theca info vault.theca # unlock and describe theca verify vault.theca # authenticate every sector and tree node theca import vault.theca --password-file pw --offset 0 < disk.img theca export vault.theca --password-file pw > disk.img theca enroll-key vault.theca --recovery-file rc # pair the key with the password and the recovery code theca info vault.theca --fido2 # password + key theca info vault.theca --recovery-file rc --fido2 # recovery code + key Secrets never go in arguments or environment variables. The password is read from the terminal with echo off, or from --password-file. The recovery code is read from --recovery-file. Both files must be regular files that only their owner can read (mode 0600 or stricter); anything else is refused. create prints the recovery code once, on standard output. If you redirect it to a file, that file gets your umask (often 0644): restrict it, or better, write the code down on paper. import reads its data from standard input, so it needs --password-file or --recovery-file. It is not one atomic transaction: on an error, the bytes written before the error are kept. enroll-key makes one discoverable credential on the key (relying party theca, credProtect 3, hmac-secret) and pairs it with the password, and with the recovery code too when --recovery-file names it. The key is touched twice: to register, then to confirm. --fido2 adds the attached key to an unlock. A key without a fingerprint asks for its PIN, read from --pin-file (mode 0600 or stricter) or from the terminal, never from an argument. Not in this version: mounting, FIDO2 on Linux and Windows, the TPM counter, and slot management on the command line (go-theca/theca#5).
data.factors#Factors:
A container is opened by one of three factors:
a password, stretched with Argon2id; a recovery code, printed once by create and never stored; a FIDO2 security key, which is never a factor alone: it always pairs with the password or with the recovery code. The policy is chosen at creation. --policy any (the default) lets the password alone, or the recovery code alone, open the container. --policy 2of3 needs two of the three: password and recovery code from the start, and a FIDO2 key (enroll-key) then pairs with each.
data.performance#Performance:
Theca is measured against C references on one core with go-scikit/refbench: libsodium for XChaCha20 and Argon2id, OpenSSL for AES-256-CTR and HMAC-SHA-256. The procedure and the cases are in bench/README.md. Ratio is Go time divided by reference time; below 1 is faster. Both runs are on commit 6d515c5 with go1.27.4, libsodium 1.0.22 and OpenSSL 4.0.2, from 2026-11-15. Medians in ns/call; the full tables, with quartiles and allocation counts, are docs/perf-table.md and docs/perf-zen4-table.md.
case Apple M4 Max (Go / ref, ratio) AMD Zen 4 (Go / ref, ratio) Sector/XChaCha20 2286 / 4143, 0.55 faster 4016 / 9195, 0.44 faster (see caveat) Sector/AES-256-CTR 459.4 / 308.9, 1.49 slower 432.7 / 357.1, 1.21 slower Sector/Tag (HMAC-SHA-256) 1493 / 1428, 1.05 slower 1691 / 1736, 0.97 faster Sector/Seal 4290 / 5935, 0.72 faster 6140 / 11330, 0.54 faster Sector/Open 4296 / 5992, 0.72 faster 6154 / 11380, 0.54 faster Argon2id t3-m64MiB-p1 9.424e+07 / 6.306e+07, 1.49 slower 6.616e+07 / 2.662e+08, 0.25 faster (see caveat) The Apple M4 Max run was at a 1-minute load of 7.22 to 7.59 (gate 8.00); the Zen 4 machine is an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X pinned to one CPU, at a load of 0.16 to 0.35. Both runs are marked valid. A gap in a row includes Theca’s own per-sector setup cost, which is a cost of the design and not of the language.
Open slower rows, each tracked as an issue:
#8: Sector/AES-256-CTR is slower than OpenSSL. #9: Sector/Tag (HMAC-SHA-256) is slower than OpenSSL. #10: Argon2id is slower than libsodium on arm64 (no NEON kernel in x/crypto/argon2). Caveat on the Zen 4 libsodium rows. On that machine libsodium’s XChaCha20 and Argon2id run far below their usual AVX2 speed (about 440 MB/s, and 4 times slower than Go’s Argon2id). The registry’s libsodium may be built without its SIMD code. Until a control with another libsodium build settles this, the “faster” verdicts in those two rows are not claims.
Source: https://github.com/go-theca/theca.
data.security#Security notes:
The threat model is DESIGN section 1. The places where the code differs from, or fixes the details of, the design are in its section 19, the implementation log; the FIDO2 design and its trade-offs are in HARDWARE-KEYS.md section 9, “H2 revised”.
Known limits, as the repository states them:
No rollback counter in the command line yet. Every command that opens a container says whether it is protected against rollback; in this version it never is, so an older copy of a container would be accepted. FIDO2 works on macOS only for now (through go-macos/fido). It was tested on a YubiKey 5, firmware 5.7.4. A reader of the FIDO2 salt can test password guesses. The salt that a key is asked for is derived from the partner factor, so for whoever reads it (a forged authenticator, a leaked log) it is a password verifier, at Argon2id cost per guess. The salts are wiped after each call and never logged (DESIGN section 19, I21). Revoked factors: older copies of a container still open with a factor that was removed (DESIGN section 19, I15). Tree area: a container at rest is indistinguishable from random except the Merkle tree area, which shows how sparse the container is (DESIGN section 19, I11).
data.theca#theca:
Theca is an encrypted container format in pure Go, with a library and a command line. It does not mount anything: the library gives an io.ReaderAt and io.WriterAt over the logical volume, and the command line creates, inspects, verifies, imports and exports containers.
Status: pre-release (v0.1 in progress, no tag yet). The format can still change. This page is written from the main branch of go-theca/theca on 2026-11-16; where it differs from the repository, the repository wins.
data.what#What it is:
From the README:
authenticated sectors: XChaCha20 xor AES-256-CTR, with HMAC-SHA-256; a Merkle tree over the sector tags, and a write-ahead journal; no magic bytes; keyslots opened by a password (Argon2id), a recovery code, or both; an optional hardware rollback counter. The design, its threat model, the sources it rests on and the decisions taken are in docs/DESIGN.md; section 0 is a one-table summary.
